collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A friend offers to toss a shell to settle a villager's choice between two jobs: let the shell decide, or catch it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been offered two jobs: helping in the gardens, or learning to build canoes. (subject.He/she) has thought about it for a week and still can't choose. (friend) picks up a shell. "Flat side, garden. Round side, canoes. I'll toss it." (friend.He/she) flicks it up into the air.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The shell spins. And while it's still in the air, (subject) realizes (subject.he/she) is hoping for the round side. It lands flat. (subject) looks at it. "Again," (subject.he/she) says. (friend) grins. "You want canoes." "I want canoes," says (subject). The shell gets put back on the beach. It did its job.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) snatches the shell out of the air before it lands. "No," (subject.he/she) says. "I don't want a shell to choose. I want to choose." (friend) shrugs. "Then choose." (subject) doesn't, not that day, not the next. A week later (subject.he/she) starts at the gardens. A season later, (subject.he/she) starts helping with canoes on the side. (subject.He/she) never fully chooses. That seems to suit (subject.him/her).
